claim_verdicts.evidence: aspnetcore 10 moniker block: "WebApplication.CreateBuilder initializes a new instance of the WebApplicationBuilder class with preconfigured defaults." Same file, WebApplicationBuilder section: "By default the WebApplicationBuilder reads configuration from multiple sources, including: appSettings.json...". fundamentals/index.md (>= 6.0): "The Program file is where: Services required by the app are configured."

Build()->WebApplication: every 10.x doc sample is `var app = builder.Build();` typed as WebApplication (webapplication10.md). Run()->Kestrel: generic-host.md: "When a host starts, it calls the StartAsync method on each IHostedService instance... In a web app, one of the IHostedService implementations is a web service that starts an HTTP server implementation." servers/index.md: "Kestrel server is the default, cross-platform HTTP server implementation." DonHang.Api registers no other server, so the default (Kestrel) is what Run() starts.

Contradicted as an absolute: dependency-injection.md L297: "Service registration methods can be used to register multiple service instances of the same service type... The second call to AddSingleton overrides the previous one when resolved as IMyDependency." So registration order does decide which implementation a request-time consumer gets when two registrations share a service type. track.yaml's own outline says "the order MOST builder.Services.Add... calls happen in"; the lesson dropped that qualifier.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: When two `builder.Services.Add...` calls register different things — as every call in this file does — the order between them only decides what is available to the app, not how a later request is answered.

claim_verdicts.evidence: mvc/controllers/routing.md (moniker ">= aspnetcore-6.0", covers 10.0) L264: "you call MapControllers to map attribute routed controllers." L414: "The route templates you define on the controller are prepended to route templates on the actions" — so [Route("api/v1/products")] + [HttpGet] gives GET /api/v1/products. fundamentals/routing.md: "Endpoints are the app's units of executable request-handling code. Endpoints are defined in the app and configured when the app starts." No aspnetcore 10 breaking change touches AddControllers/MapControllers.

fundamentals/routing.md: "Routing is responsible for matching incoming HTTP requests and dispatching those requests to the app's executable endpoints." "An endpoint is something that can be: Selected, by matching the URL and HTTP method. Executed, by running the delegate." "UseRouting adds route matching to the middleware pipeline... UseEndpoints adds endpoint execution to the middleware pipeline. It runs the delegate associated with the selected endpoint." Registration is startup-time ("configured when the app starts"); execution is per matched request.

Documented part: migration/22-to-30.md "MVC service registration": "The following example adds support for controllers and API-related features, but not views or pages. The API template uses this code: services.AddControllers();" Not in the pinned-version mirror: that MapControllers() cannot find controllers without it (the runtime throws, but no doc page states it). I could not run the app to show the exception — the lab is not up and Program.cs needs a DB.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `AddControllers()` registers the services controllers need; without it, `app.MapControllers()` further down has no controller classes like `ProductsController` to map.

claim_verdicts.evidence: `git -C examples/don-hang show stage-1:DonHang.Api/Program.cs | cat -n`: L52 `var app = builder.Build();`, L74 `app.Run();` is the last line (file is 74 lines). Between them: L57-62 the migration scope block (MigrationBaseline.ApplyIfNeeded + context.Database.Migrate()) and L67-72 UseMiddleware/UseCors/UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization/MapControllers. Both lesson code blocks (lines=10-20, lines=52-74) match the tagged source character-for-character.

Repo capture at the tag, outputs/stage-1/scripts/backend/auth-and-orders.txt: "products (no sign-in needed):" then the JSON list — ProductsController has no [Authorize]. ProductsController.List() runs `await db.Products.Select(...).ToListAsync()` per call; Program.cs registers no output cache, so nothing is computed at startup. Host reachability: docker-compose.yml publishes "8080:8080" on the lab box, Caddyfile `:8080 { handle /api/v1/* { reverse_proxy api:8080 } }`. I could not run the lab live (docker up, lab containers not running).

issues.quote: turns each attribute-routed method on them into a method-and-path pair Kestrel can route a matching request to
issues.text: Kestrel does not route. fundamentals/routing.md: "Routing is responsible for matching incoming HTTP requests and dispatching those requests to the app's executable endpoints" and "UseRouting adds route matching to the middleware pipeline. This middleware looks at the set of endpoints defined in the app, and selects the best match based on the request." Kestrel is the HTTP server that reads the connection; endpoint matching is the routing middleware's job. The previous lesson taught Kestrel as the server, so this sentence teaches a wrong division of labour.
issues.fix: Rewrite as: "...turns each attribute-routed method on them into a method-and-path pair the app can match an incoming request to." Do not name Kestrel as the thing that routes anywhere in the lesson.

issues.quote: the order these registrations happen in does not decide how a later request is answered; it only decides what is available for the app to use
issues.text: False as an absolute. dependency-injection.md L297: "The second call to AddSingleton overrides the previous one when resolved as IMyDependency and adds to the previous one when multiple services are resolved via IEnumerable<IMyDependency>." When two registrations share a service type, the later one wins at resolution time and that does change how a request is answered. The track.yaml outline says "the order MOST builder.Services.Add... calls happen in"; the lesson dropped the qualifier in four places (§4, §5, §6 first misconception, §8 line 2).
issues.fix: Add the missing condition wherever the claim appears: say that the order between `Services.Add...` calls that register different things — as every call in this file does — is free. Change §6 "only the `Services.Add...` order is free to vary" and §8 line 2 the same way; update claim 3 in .meta.json to the narrowed wording.

issues.quote: None of these lines decide how any one request gets answered — swapping their order changes nothing a client would ever see
issues.text: Not true of the block as quoted. Two of its lines are `var connectionString = builder.Configuration.GetConnectionString("Default") ?? throw ...` and `builder.Services.AddDonHangInfrastructure(connectionString);`. Swapping those two is a C# compile error (use of a local before its declaration), so the app never starts — a very visible change. The freedom claimed only holds among the `builder.Services.Add...` calls.
issues.fix: Scope the sentence to the registration calls: "None of the `builder.Services.Add...` lines decide how any one request gets answered — reordering them among themselves changes nothing a client would ever see...". Keep the `connectionString` local out of the claim (it is ordinary C#: the variable must be declared before it is used).

issues.quote: Calling `builder.Build()` closes that registration phase
issues.text: Unlisted claim: it is not in .meta.json's claims ledger, and it is read as a runtime guarantee (registering after Build() is rejected). No page in the pinned aspnetcore 10 documentation mirror states that the service collection becomes unmodifiable after WebApplicationBuilder.Build(); I could not run the app to show the exception. It is also repeated in quiz q1's correct-answer explanation ("`Build()` closes the registration phase").
issues.fix: Either weaken to a statement about this file only — "`builder.Build()` ends the registration half of Program.cs and produces the `WebApplication`" (and the same in q1's explanation) — or keep the strong wording, add it to `claims` with `kind: behavior`, and back it with a documented sentence or a run that shows the failure.

issues.quote: Between `Build()` and `Run()`, Program.cs wires up the steps every incoming request will pass through before reaching your code
issues.text: In this file that region is not only wiring: lines 57-62 open a scope and run `MigrationBaseline.ApplyIfNeeded(context)` + `context.Database.Migrate()`, which is startup-only work no request passes through. §5 later admits this ("what runs against the database"), so §4 as written contradicts the code block the reader is about to see.
issues.fix: Write: "Between `Build()` and `Run()`, Program.cs does the rest of its startup work — including wiring up the steps every incoming request will pass through before reaching your code."

issues.quote: An endpoint is a method-and-path pair mapped to handler code with a call like `app.MapGet`
issues.text: The scope contract (track.yaml, outline item 3 and misconception 2) names `app.MapGet`; DonHang.Api has no minimal-API endpoint, so the lesson correctly used `app.MapControllers()` instead. The adaptation is accurate for aspnetcore 10 (mvc/controllers/routing.md: "Call MapControllers to map attribute routed controllers"), but the outline and the lesson now disagree, and the next reviewer or regeneration will hit the same conflict.
issues.fix: Update track.yaml for this lesson: outline item 3 -> "...mapped to handler code by a call like `app.MapControllers()`", misconception 2 -> "`app.MapControllers()`'s handler code runs immediately...". Do not change the lesson.

issues.quote: turns each attribute-routed method on them into a method-and-path pair
issues.text: "attribute-routed" carries the whole mechanism of this lesson (it is what decides that `ProductsController.List()` answers GET /api/v1/products) but is never explained, is not in `vocab: [endpoint]`, and is not in glossary.yaml. The quoted code block does not show ProductsController, so the reader never sees `[Route("api/v1/products")]` or `[HttpGet]`.
issues.fix: Add a half-sentence gloss on first use, e.g. "attribute-routed — the path is written on the class and the method themselves, as `[Route(\"api/v1/products\")]` and `[HttpGet]`", or add the term to `vocab` in track.yaml and glossary.yaml.

issues.quote: False, because `builder.Services.Add...` calls only make things available; the order between two such calls does not decide how any request is later handled.
issues.text: The key (c) is correct for the pair asked about — `OrderService` and `JwtTokenService` are different service types, so swapping them changes nothing. But the option's justification is the same over-general rule flagged above: for two registrations of the same service type the later one wins (dependency-injection.md L297), so the stated reason is not universally true.
issues.fix: Narrow option c to: "False, because these two `builder.Services.Add...` calls register different services; the order between them does not decide how any request is later handled." Keep the answer key as ["c"].

issues.quote: turns each attribute-routed method on them into a method-and-path pair Kestrel can route a matching request to

issues.fix: In the same sentence, gloss it once: "...classes like `ProductsController` — classes whose methods are written to answer requests — and turns each...".
